parsed.summary: This paper decomposes the generalization gap of dermatology AI models when deployed in resource-constrained settings into two components: skin tone and disease-distribution shift. By evaluating a cancer-trained baseline and three foundation models on tone-stratified and disease-shifted datasets, the authors find that disease-distribution shift is the dominant driver of performance degradation. They show that this degradation is representational and that starting with a dermatology foundation model allows for cheap adaptation with minimal labeled data.

chk_problem.value: Decomposing the generalization gap of dermatology AI models when deployed in resource-constrained settings, specifically separating the effects of skin tone and disease-distribution shift.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet are increasingly proposed for deployment in resource-constrained settings (RCS) whose patients differ from the training population along two confounded axes at once: skin tone and disease distribution.

chk_method.value: Evaluating a cancer-trained baseline and three foundation models as frozen feature extractors using linear probing, label-free representation-quality analysis (kNN neighbor purity), and low-compute adaptation.
chk_method.paper_quote: We evaluate a cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019), two open dermatology foundation models (DermLIP, MONET), and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as frozen feature extractors, probing them on a tone-stratified but disease-matched dataset (Diverse Dermatology Images, DDI) and a disease-shifted, tone-diverse dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, SCIN).

chk_data.value: Four public datasets: HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 (in-domain reference), Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI, tone-stratified), and Skin Condition Image Network (SCIN, tone-diverse, non-neoplastic).
chk_data.paper_quote: We use four public datasets, each assigned a specific experimental role (Table 1).

chk_setup.value: Extracting frozen embeddings from the models and evaluating them using L2-regularized logistic-regression probes with patient-level GroupShuffleSplit (70/30), label-free kNN neighbor purity (k=10), and few-shot probes (10 examples/class).
chk_setup.paper_quote: We fit an L2-regularized logistic-regression probe on standardized frozen features, using patient-level GroupShuffleSplit (70/30) to prevent leakage, and report balanced accuracy.

chk_primary_result.value: The cancer baseline's balanced accuracy degrades from 0.62 in-domain to 0.21 on SCIN (unfamiliar conditions), whereas the within-disease skin-tone gap on DDI is comparatively small (0.10-0.18).
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: In our setting, disease-distribution shift contributes more than skin tone: the cancer baseline degrades sharply from its in-domain performance to unfamiliar conditions (a drop from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy across clinical categories), a far larger effect than the within-disease skin-tone gap, which is comparatively small (0.10-0.18) and did not show a consistent direction.

chk_secondary_result.value: Under label-free representation-quality analysis, the cancer baseline's features barely cluster unfamiliar conditions (kNN neighbor-purity lift +0.06 over chance), whereas dermatology-pretrained features retain more structure (+0.23).
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Using a label-free representation-quality analysis, we show this collapse is representational, not merely an artifact of disjoint label spaces: cancer-specialized features barely cluster unfamiliar conditions (kNN neighbor-purity lift +0.06 over chance), whereas dermatology-pretrained features retain substantially more transferable structure (+0.23).

chk_baseline.value: A cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019) and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as a no-dermatology-knowledge control.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: We evaluate a cancer-trained baseline (ResNet-50 fine-tuned on HAM10000 and ISIC 2019), two open dermatology foundation models (DermLIP, MONET), and a general-purpose vision model (DINOv3) as frozen feature extractors, probing them on a tone-stratified but disease-matched dataset (Diverse Dermatology Images, DDI) and a disease-shifted, tone-diverse dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, SCIN).

chk_conclusion.value: Disease-distribution shift is the dominant driver of the generalization gap compared to skin tone, and starting with a dermatology foundation model enables cheap adaptation to local conditions with minimal labeled data.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: Using only public data and free-tier compute, we decomposed the dermatology-AI generalization gap and found disease-distribution shift to dominate skin tone, traced the effect to a representational deficit in cancer-specialized models, and found that cheap adaptation is most effective when the starting representation already encodes the target conditions.

chk_limitation.value: DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies rather than resource-constrained settings (RCS) cohorts, meaning deployment-oriented conclusions are inferential and require validation on genuine RCS cohorts.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: First and most importantly, DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies used to isolate each factor, not RCS-collected data; our RCS conclusions are therefore inferential, and validation on genuinely RCS-collected cohorts is important future work.
